video.description:
Learn to explain how to mix SwiftUI and UIKit: UIHostingController, UIViewRepresentable & Coordinator, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
UIHostingController - A view controller that shows a SwiftUI view inside a UIKit app.
UIViewRepresentable - A protocol that wraps a UIKit view, so you can use it inside SwiftUI.
Coordinator - An object inside a representable that receives UIKit delegate calls and talks back to SwiftUI.

landscape.hook: Can you explain UIHostingController, UIViewRepresentable and Coordinator in English?

dialogue.title: UIKit meets SwiftUI

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our old app is UIKit, but my new screen is SwiftUI.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a UIHostingController. It is a view controller that shows a SwiftUI view in UIKit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote `UIHostingController(rootView: Map())`, and it works.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Great. A UIHostingController can be pushed like any view controller.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now the opposite. I need a UIKit map view inside SwiftUI.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wrap it in a UIViewRepresentable. It is a protocol that turns a UIKit view into a SwiftUI view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In `Map`, I return the view in `makeUIView`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, and SwiftUI calls `updateUIView` when the state changes. Every UIViewRepresentable needs both.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I handle delegate callbacks from the UIKit view?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a Coordinator. It is an object that receives the delegate calls.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And how does SwiftUI create the Coordinator?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In `makeCoordinator`. Then you read it from `context`.
